generator.params.basal_area.note: The leaf area its `basal` look draws on an organ 1 m long (visual forms Skill 1, 2026-10-14; plantc atlas), so it shades with what it shows: the look now takes its card from the taxa's characters, where before it drew the generic card (0.235); drawn again with the teeth the kingdom's margin rule gives it (2026-10-16).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): stems mostly 4-8 dm; subsp. elongata, which FNA now places partly in S. lepida's circle, 3-10(15) dm. Replaces the spec's 0.3-1.0 (high 1.5), taken from elongata; see disagreements.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall herb spreading into patches of leafy stems with narrow, toothed leaves and plumes of small golden-yellow heads. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.1 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaves; golden plumes.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Flora of North America's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): 14 to 800 or more heads in paniculiform arrays, broadly thyrsiform or pyramidal, sometimes secund, the lower branches of var. salebrosa arching to recurved.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its array drawn head by head (spec rework L1c): its kind from its characters, by the rule at the flowering plants; a pyramid of 12 arching branches of 18 heads each, by eye (a mid-sized plant's of the Flora of North America's 14 to 800), each head about 7 mm across with 13 yellow rays (the Burke Herbarium: rays 10 to 17, usually 13, 1 to 3 mm long; involucres 2 to 5 mm high). From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. The plant stands as tall as before: its stems end where the array begins.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): stems from creeping rhizomes (as in elongata).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): elongata's leaves 5-12 cm long, 1-2 cm wide; S. lepida's scarcely reduced up to the panicle.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): leaves 1-2 cm wide (elongata).

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): leaves elliptic-lanceolate (elongata: lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate), triple-nerved.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): leaves usually sharply serrate-dentate (elongata: sharply serrate to entire).

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): leaves toothed only.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): leaves tapering to the base, nearly uniform; no petiole described (lower leaves of the genus key deciduous).

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): involucre 3.5-5 mm high (elongata); in S. lepida not very imbricate, the outer phyllaries over half as long as the inner.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): ray florets mostly about 13, little longer than the disc (elongata; genus key: 8-13 in this group).

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Solidago lepida (p. 293), which it calls otherwise like S. canadensis subsp. elongata (p. 292): July to September (elongata: July to October).

appearance.organs.flower.shape.involucre.note: The involucre drawn about 1.2 times as tall as the disc is wide, so its height comes to the flora's 3.5 to 5 mm (spec rework E1); the daisy family's rule sets it from the involucre's height and width, and no flora read gives this goldenrod's width.
